source.locator: Only call Hooks at the top level
source.paraphrase: Call Hooks unconditionally at the top level of a component or custom Hook so every render runs them in the same order.

invariants.why: A Hook inside a branch runs on some renders and not others, so every Hook after it reads the wrong slot.
invariants.fixHint: Move the Hook call above the branch and put only its result inside the condition.
invariants.avoid: A custom Hook is still a plain function: the rule only fires inside a branch or loop, so a helper without JSX is not flagged. The condition of an if or a ternary runs on every render and is not a branch. A Hook on the right of &&, ||, or ?? is. A Hook inside a function nested in a branch is that function's own top-level call.

source.paraphrase: An effect callback returns either nothing or a cleanup function. An async callback returns a promise, so the cleanup protocol cannot run.

invariants.why: React treats the returned promise as a cleanup function that never runs, and rejections escape the effect.
invariants.fixHint: Define an async function inside the effect and void it, or move the work into an event handler.
invariants.avoid: An async helper declared inside a synchronous effect callback is fine; only the callback itself must stay synchronous.

source.locator: Do not update state during render
source.paraphrase: React permits guarded updates of the current component during render to track previous renders. Unconditional updates can loop.

invariants.why: The matcher cannot resolve setter bindings or prove a guarded update converges. A setX name alone does not establish a defect.
invariants.fixHint: Review whether this is a React setter and whether a guarded update converges before changing it.
invariants.avoid: Guarded previous-render updates are documented as valid. Ordinary functions named setX are also matched; keep this heuristic off until bindings and control flow are resolved.

source.locator: Only call Hooks at the top level
source.paraphrase: Hooks cannot be called inside callbacks passed to iterators, effects, timers, or promise handlers.

invariants.why: A callback can run outside render or a different number of times, so React cannot preserve the Hook call order.
invariants.fixHint: Move the Hook to the top level of the component or custom Hook and pass its result into the callback.
invariants.avoid: Renaming the callback does not turn it into a component. Components passed to memo remain valid and are not matched.
